study_identification_part.si4_title: Developmental trajectories of neuroanatomical alterations associated with the 16p11.2 Copy Number Variations

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states research objectives and hypotheses. The paper explicitly describes the purpose of applying normative modeling: (1) to characterize age-related effects of 16p11.2 CNVs by normalizing volumes using a large normative developmental dataset, (2) to investigate when brain alterations appear during development and whether they evolve with age. The abstract states 'we aim at characterizing age-related effects of 16p11.2 copy number variants by analyzing a group with a broad age range including younger individuals. A large normative developmental dataset was used to accurately adjust for effects of age.' The introduction further elaborates: 'we hypothesized that the established pattern of brain alterations associated with 16p11.2 CNVs might appear during early childhood. We aimed to characterize brain growth in 16p11.2 CNVs carriers by comparing global and regional developmental trajectories to those of healthy children.' Both criteria are satisfied.

We aimed to characterize brain growth in 16p11.2 CNVs carriers by comparing global and regional developmental trajectories to those of healthy children.'
